flags.why: Mót also commonly describes an urgent need to defecate, which the entry omits ([dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/m%C3%B3t)).
flags.fix: to need to defecate urgently; tags: colloquial

flags.why: The literal sense means causing intense, prolonged heat, rather than a fire burning fiercely ([dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-nung%20n%E1%BA%A5u)).
flags.fix: to subject to intense, prolonged heat

flags.why: Ngọn lửa nung nấu trong lò incorrectly uses nung nấu as an intransitive verb meaning to burn fiercely.
flags.fix: Cái nắng nung nấu suốt ngày. = The sun beat down intensely all day.

flags.why: Tày describes a blunt point, so using it for a knife's inability to cut confuses it with a dull cutting edge ([dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-t%C3%A0y)).
flags.fix: Đầu kim này tày quá, không đâm xuyên qua vải được. = This needle's point is too blunt to pierce the fabric.

flags.why: Learners are much more likely to encounter the comparison sense in expressions such as tày trời and tày đình than the blunt-point sense.
The comparison sense remains current in common expressions such as tày trời and tày đình, so dated is misleading.
